newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Depositors besiege Bulgaria State Savings Bank.
newsitem.headline: Depositors besiege Bulgaria State Savings Bank.

text.p: Panicked depositors queued outside branches of Bulgaria's State Savings Bank (SSB) around the country on Tuesday to withdraw their savings before the collapse of the local currency eroded them any further.

"I am always very scared when politicians and bankers say on television that everything is under control because it is always the other way round," said one pensioner in a queue of mainly elderly people outside the SSB's central Sofia office.
Many said they did not believe the currency board proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would end the crisis quickly and they wanted to convert their savings to dollars.
"I know only one thing, there is no point in trying to save money, so I will close my account and I will buy some clothes for the winter," said pensioner Ivanka Drumeva, 58.
Depositors said they had panicked after hearing reports of queues at the bank, Bulgaria's biggest savings institution, and did not trust official assurances that all was well.

"It is obvious that levs will not be worth even the paper they are printed on in a couple of months. So I think the best idea is to change all money into dollars," said Gergana Ilieva, 26, an assistant in a private company.
"With or without a currency board you can always buy everything with dollars."

Under the currency board scheme, the amount of levs in circulation must be exactly matched by the central bank's hard currency reserves. It has been used by Argentina, Estonia and Lithuania to restore confidence and help defeat hyperinflation.
SSB head Bistra Dimitrova told Reuters about four billion levs ($14.63 million) had been withdrawn from the bank since early last week, but queues were starting to die down.
"There is a trend of declining pressure from depositors," she said.
She said she had ordered the lifting of a limit of 200,000 levs for withdrawals without prior notice on Tuesday.
She said one branch had large queues because it was serving former depositors of Agrobusinessbank, one of 13 illiquid banks for which the central bank is seeking insolvency in court.
The lev fell to 283-285 to the dollar on the interbank market and 292-295 on the cash market on Tuesday. The currency started the year at 70 to the dollar.
The government is holding consultations with political parties and trade unions on the IMF-proposed introduction of a currency board to stabilise the economy and curb inflation.

The proposal has the backing of Socialist Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, but the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) hardened its criticism on Tuesday, saying it would not support such a measure while the Socialists remained in power.

"If the currency board system is introduced under the Socialist government, Bulgaria will miss its last chance to end the crisis, even with the support of the IMF," said Yordan Sokolov, head of the UDF parliamentary group.
Introduction of a currency board must be approved by parliament, in which the Socialists have a majority. ($1=273.43 Leva)
